title: game_timeline --turns breaks on v7 exports without snapshot ts
description:
The `scripts/analysis/game_timeline.py` turn filter silently misclassifies every event as the final turn on v7 exports whose `snapshots[]` entries do not include `ts`.

Evidence:
- While deep-analyzing `game_20260309_173923`, `uv run python scripts/analysis/game_timeline.py game_20260309_173923` printed 457 events, but `uv run python scripts/analysis/game_timeline.py game_20260309_173923 --turns 7-9 -v` printed `(0 events shown)` even though turn-8 combat is present throughout the export and raw logs.
- `website/public/games/game_20260309_173923.json` has 304 `snapshots`, but the snapshot objects only contain keys like `turn`, `phase`, `step`, and `seq` — no `ts` field.
- The current helper at `scripts/analysis/game_timeline.py:66` compares `snap.get("ts", "") <= ts`. When `ts` is missing, that falls back to `""`, so every snapshot compares as earlier than every event timestamp and `find_turn_at_ts()` returns the last snapshot turn (17) for all 459 `llmEvents`.
- The filter at `scripts/analysis/game_timeline.py:390` then drops every event outside the requested range, making `--turns` unusable on these exports.

Suggested fix: stop deriving event turns from missing snapshot timestamps. Either map `llmEvents` to turns using explicit event metadata / snapshot indices, or fail fast with a clear error when the export lacks `snapshots[].ts` instead of silently treating all events as the final turn.
